title: Can Your Group Take On the Fish River Canyon Hike? Permits, Water and Fitness for Clubs
meta_title: Fish River Canyon Hike as a Group: Permits and Water
meta_description: Planning the Fish River Canyon hike with a club? Group rules, medical certificates, the May-September season, water and logistics from Hobas to /Ai-/Ais.
excerpt: The Fish River Canyon hike is an 85 km, five-day trek with no facilities. Here is how clubs and groups handle the permits, season, water and logistics.
content:
The Fish River Canyon hike is a self-supported trek of about 85 km over four to five days, from Hobas to /Ai-/Ais in southern Namibia, open only from May to mid-September. Groups need at least three people, a doctor's fitness certificate for each hiker and a booking with Namibia Wildlife Resorts.

For a club, the hard part of a Fish River Canyon hike is everything around the walking: matching fitness, paperwork, water and the long drive south. This guide covers the rules, the season, the two ways to do it and how we set up club and society safaris so that the whole group reaches the hot springs together.

Quick Facts

  • Distance: About 85 km (roughly 80 km with shortcuts), Hobas to /Ai-/Ais
  • Time: Four to five days on the canyon floor
  • Season: 1 May to 15 September, subject to water levels (checked November 2026)
  • Group rules: Minimum three hikers; a signed medical certificate for everyone
  • Facilities: None on the trail: no toilets, no fires, no fixed campsites
  • Booking: Through Namibia Wildlife Resorts (NWR), well ahead of the season
  • Who it suits: Fit, self-sufficient groups; children under 13 are not allowed on the main trail

What Does the Fish River Canyon Hike Involve for a Group?

The Fish River Canyon hike involves a steep descent from the rim near Hobas, then four or five days of walking along the riverbed to /Ai-/Ais. Each hiker carries food, a stove, a sleeping bag and water treatment, and the group sleeps on sand banks with no facilities at all.

The canyon sits inside the /Ai-/Ais-Richtersveld Transfrontier Park and is often described as the largest in Africa. The Fish River Canyon hike is rarely technical but it is relentless: boulder fields early on, deep sand and river crossings that can be knee-deep after a wet year.

The descent at the start is the steepest part. Chains and handrails help, and official guidance says it takes 45 minutes to three hours. A group should plan for the slow end of that range.

The route at a glance

Distances on the Fish River Canyon hike are measured from Hobas. There are only two emergency exits, so the stretch between them is where self-reliance matters most.

PointApprox. distanceWhy it matters for a group
First emergency exit14 kmLast easy way out if someone struggles on day one
Palm (Sulphur) Springs16 kmPopular first or second camp; the water tastes and smells of sulphur
Table MountainAbout 40 kmRoughly halfway; a good check on the group's pace
Four Finger RockAbout 60 kmClassic viewpoint; shortcuts around here save time
Second emergency exitAbout 70 kmA vehicle can reach this point in an emergency
/Ai-/AisAbout 85 to 90 kmHot springs, showers and transport back to Hobas

For shorter walks from a lodge each night, see our guide to a Namibia hiking safari.

How Many People Can Hike Together, and What Paperwork Is Needed?

A group on the Fish River Canyon hike must have at least three people, and there is an upper limit on how many can start together. Every hiker needs a medical certificate signed by a doctor, and children under 13 are not allowed on the main trail.

The maximum group size has changed over the years, so confirm it in writing when you book your Fish River Canyon hike rather than relying on an old forum post.

Minimum numbers, medical certificates and age

The three-person minimum is a safety rule: if one person is hurt, one stays while another goes for help. It matters when a group splits, because each part must still number at least three.

Medical certificates are checked at Hobas before the Fish River Canyon hike starts. Collect them centrally, check names match passports and carry printed copies. A missing certificate means that person does not walk.

Booking with Namibia Wildlife Resorts

Permits for the Fish River Canyon hike are issued by Namibia Wildlife Resorts, which also runs the Hobas and /Ai-/Ais camps. In July 2026 its online booking system was unavailable and requests went to its reservations team by email. The NWR notice on the Fish River Canyon trail is the best place to check the current status.

Permit fees for the Fish River Canyon hike are charged per person, with park fees on top. They are revised often, so confirm current amounts with NWR before collecting money from members.

When Is the Fish River Canyon Open, and How Reliable Is the Season?

The Fish River Canyon is open for hiking from 1 May to 15 September, the cooler, drier southern winter. Outside those dates the trail is closed because canyon heat becomes dangerous. Within the season, high water can delay the start or close the trail for weeks.

Recent seasons show why groups need flexibility. In April 2025 NWR postponed the hiking season because of high water levels. In 2026 the trail opened late, on 15 May, after April rain. June floods then forced an evacuation of hikers, and NWR reopened the trail on 17 July 2026.

MonthConditionsGroup verdict
MaySeason opens; water levels can still be high after a wet summerGood if the trail is open; keep a back-up plan
JuneCool days, cold nights; winter rain is unusual but possibleVery good, with warm sleeping bags
JulyColdest nights, clear skies, shortest daysBest for comfort on the trail; popular, so book early
AugustDry and mild, nights still cold, warming by month endVery good; book early
Early SeptemberWarming quickly; pools may be low and water harder to findFine for fit, experienced groups; start each day at first light
Mid-September to AprilTrail closed because of heatNot possible on the main trail

The same winter months suit Etosha and the dunes; see the best time to visit Namibia.

Self-Supported or Luggage-Free: Which Version Suits Your Group?

Groups can either do the full self-supported Fish River Canyon hike on the NWR trail or walk a shorter, guided luggage-free trail in the private Gondwana Canyon Park north of the main viewpoint. The first is the classic expedition; the second suits mixed fitness and shorter trips.

According to its operator, the Gondwana Canyon Park trails run from about April to September, take 4 to 14 people and range from the Klipspringer Trail (17 km, three nights) to the Zebra and Fish Eagle trails (35 km over three or four nights). Gear is moved between simple self-catering camps, so hikers walk with a daypack. Confirm details when you enquire.

FeatureNWR main trailGondwana luggage-free trails
DistanceAbout 85 km17 to 35 km
Nights on the trailThree to four, wild campingThree or four, in basic camps
What you carryEverything: food, stove, tent or bivvy, waterA daypack; gear is moved for you
Group sizeMinimum three; maximum set by NWR4 to 14 people (per the operator)
Best forFit, experienced backpackersMixed-ability clubs, first multi-day hike

Who should do the full Fish River Canyon hike?

The full Fish River Canyon hike suits groups where everyone has carried a heavy pack for several days before and is happy with no toilets and no phone signal. If members have never done a multi-day trek, train them or choose the luggage-free option.

Some clubs split: strong walkers do the Fish River Canyon hike while others take a shorter trail, and everyone meets at /Ai-/Ais. The same idea works on mountains, as in our guide to a Kilimanjaro group climb.

How Do You Plan the Logistics for a Group Hike?

Planning a group Fish River Canyon hike means sorting three things before anything else: transport to Hobas and back from /Ai-/Ais, rooming at the rest camps either side, and a water and food plan everyone follows. The canyon is remote, so these choices decide how the trip feels.

Hobas is a long day's drive from Windhoek, mostly on tar via Keetmanshoop. For a group we split it over two days so nobody starts the Fish River Canyon hike tired, and suitcases travel separately to /Ai-/Ais.

Transport runs from /Ai-/Ais back to Hobas, but a private group is better off with its own driver meeting it at the finish, who is also a support contact near the 70 km exit. Book beds at /Ai-/Ais early.

How group pricing works

Group costs split into fixed and per-person items. Vehicles, drivers and guides cost the same for 8 or 12 people, so the price per head drops as numbers rise until another vehicle is needed. Permits, meals and rooms are per person, which is why we quote groups personally.

A private group beats joining strangers: you set the pace and the start date, and keep together on a trail with only two ways out. How Should the Group Train and Pack?

The group should train with full packs on rough, hilly ground for at least two months, and plan water before anything else. Dehydration, not injury, is the most common reason hikers are evacuated from the canyon, especially early and late in the season.

Recent seasons brought afternoons near 40°C, low pools and a helicopter rescue of a group short of drinkable water. On the Fish River Canyon hike, walk early, rest at midday and treat every refill, including sulphur spring water.

Share the load: one gas stove per three or four people (fires are banned), a first-aid kit per team, a satellite messenger and a headlamp each. Carry all rubbish out.

After the Fish River Canyon hike, most groups want animals. Our 5-day Sossusvlei and Etosha tour adds dunes and game drives, and clubs keen on people and rock art can follow with the 6-day Namibia culture tour for clubs. Browse more Namibia safari packages to build the full trip.

Insider Tips

  • Hold two start dates: If the river is high, a second date a week later can save the trip
  • Pace by the slowest: Put the slowest walker second in line and the strongest at the back
  • Collect certificates early: Gather every medical certificate six weeks out, with copies
  • Name a water lead: One person tracks pools, refills and treatment each day
  • Start in the dark: Leave camp at first light and stop before the midday heat
  • Book /Ai-/Ais rooms: A bed and hot shower at the finish is worth reserving early

Frequently Asked Questions

How many people can do the Fish River Canyon hike together?

The Fish River Canyon hike needs at least three people per group, and there is a cap on how many can start together. Older official fact sheets give 40, while newer guidance quotes fewer, so confirm the limit with Namibia Wildlife Resorts. Large clubs walk better as two teams.

Do you need a medical certificate for the Fish River Canyon hike?

Yes. Every hiker on the Fish River Canyon hike must hand in a medical certificate signed by a doctor, confirming they are fit enough for a multi-day wilderness trek. It is checked at Hobas before you start. Ask the doctor to use the wording Namibia Wildlife Resorts requests, and keep copies for the whole group in one folder.

When is the Fish River Canyon hiking season?

The Fish River Canyon hiking season normally runs from 1 May to 15 September, because summer heat in the canyon is dangerous. High water can delay or interrupt it: in 2026 the trail opened on 15 May after April rain, closed again after June floods and reopened on 17 July. Book early, but keep plans flexible.

How long does the Fish River Canyon hike take?

The Fish River Canyon hike takes four to five days for most groups. The route runs about 85 km from Hobas to the /Ai-/Ais hot springs, or nearer 80 km if you use the sandy shortcuts. A group moves at the speed of its slowest member, so plan five days unless everyone is a seasoned backpacker.

Is there an easier way for a group to hike the Fish River Canyon?

Yes. The private Gondwana Canyon Park, north of the main viewpoint, has guided luggage-free trails of 17 to 35 km over three or four nights, for groups of 4 to 14. Gear is moved between simple self-catering camps, so hikers carry only a daypack. It suits mixed-fitness clubs better than the full canyon trail.

Final Thoughts

The Fish River Canyon hike rewards groups that plan around the short winter season, paperwork for every member and 85 km with no facilities. Keep a spare start date in case of high water, and choose a luggage-free trail if fitness is mixed.
